source_text: Sessions emphasized an "epidemic" of unnecessary procedures, with estimates citing millions of annual cases globally, and critiqued medical literature for underreporting harms while overemphasizing unproven preventive benefits, such as against urinary tract infections, where absolute risk reductions were small (e.g., from 1% to 0.1% in neonates per some studies). [25]
